title: Qilimanjaro Secures €19.6 Million ($21.9 Million USD) Series A First Close to Industrialize Multimodal Fluxonium Systems - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Spanish quantum hardware maker Qilimanjaro closed a €19.6M Series A first close from Indra Group (€10M) and state fund SETT (€9.6M) to industrialize fluxonium-qubit systems that combine analog and digital QPUs with HPC. The funding mix underlines European defense and sovereign interest in quantum.

themes.theme: Series A structure and sovereign capital

insights.claim: Qilimanjaro's €19.6M ($21.9M) Series A first close is split between Indra Group via IndraMind (€10.0M) and Spain's SETT through the PERTE Chip microelectronics facility (€9.6M), with Avançsa and others to follow at a Q4 2026 final close.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Round is entirely strategic and state capital rather than venture; further size depends on the Q4 final close.

insights.claim: Indra's participation through IndraMind signals growing European defense-sector interest in quantum-accelerated AI and secure communications, co-developing sovereign AI, defense and cyber-resilient dual-use technology.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defense primes entering as quantum investors points to sovereign procurement as a funding source for European quantum startups.
insights.locator: Indra's participation through its IndraMind unit

insights.claim: Qilimanjaro uses fluxonium superconducting qubits, offering longer coherence times and better resilience to flux noise, rather than relying solely on conventional transmons, and integrates analog and digital QPUs with classical HPC for optimization, simulation and defense AI workloads.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A differentiated qubit choice and hybrid HPC integration is the company's claim for standing out among superconducting vendors.
insights.locator: Rather than relying solely on conventional transmon

insights.claim: Qilimanjaro's hybrid deployment model is described as already operational, building on an analog quantum system at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center and a multimodal Quantum Data Center launched in Barcelona.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Existing deployments give some customer-proof; the capital funds chip fabrication and manufacturing scale-up.
insights.locator: Indra's participation through its IndraMind unit
